title: SWEET32 medium-strength cipher support on a production virtual machine

case_origin.source: Tenable vulnerability export supplied for thesis experiment

source_references.plugin_name: SSL Medium Strength Cipher Suites Supported (SWEET32)

experimental_selection_reason: Medium-severity weak-encryption finding on a source asset marked Critical; selected to represent cryptographic configuration risk.

finding.plugin_name: SSL Medium Strength Cipher Suites Supported (SWEET32)
finding.synopsis: The remote service supports the use of medium strength SSL ciphers.
finding.description:
The remote host supports the use of SSL ciphers that offer medium strength encryption. Nessus regards medium strength as any encryption that uses key lengths at least 64 bits and less than 112 bits, or else that uses the 3DES encryption suite.

Note that it is considerably easier to circumvent medium strength encryption if the attacker is on the same physical network.
finding.recommended_remediation: Reconfigure the affected application if possible to avoid use of medium strength ciphers.
